items.rationale: Sub-account creation (agent.team.testnet) isolates balances and keys so one compromised agent cannot spend another agent's funds. Command: near account create-account fund-myself agent.team.testnet '1 NEAR' autogenerate-new-keypair save-to-keychain sign-as team.testnet network-config testnet sign-with-keychain send

items.rationale: A function-call access key can only call the listed contract and cannot transfer NEAR or deploy code, which limits the blast radius. Command: near account add-key agent.team.testnet grant-function-call-access --allowance '0.25 NEAR' --contract-account-id hub.team.testnet --function-names 'place_bid, submit_work' autogenerate-new-keypair save-to-keychain network-config testnet sign-with-keychain send

items.rationale: Method restrictions mean a leaked worker key cannot call verify_bounty or select_winner; list only the methods the role needs and test that other calls fail.

items.rationale: Allowance limits cap how much gas a stolen key can burn. The allowance cannot be raised later, so rotate the key when it runs out instead of granting an unlimited allowance.

items.rationale: Removing full-access keys from agent sub-accounts means the only remaining key is the restricted one. Command: near account delete-keys agent.team.testnet public-keys ed25519:<pk> network-config testnet sign-with-keychain send. Keep recovery on the parent account.

items.rationale: Key rotation: add the new function-call key with near-api-js account.addFunctionCallAccessKey(), switch the agent over, then delete the old key so a leaked key has a short lifetime.

items.rationale: Load private keys from environment variables (.env.local, gitignored) and ship only .env.example; judges and attackers both scan git history.

sections.checklist:
1. Give every agent its own sub-account - Sub-account creation (agent.team.testnet) isolates balances and keys so one compromised agent cannot spend another agent's funds. Command: near account create-account fund-myself agent.team.testnet '1 NEAR' autogenerate-new-keypair save-to-keychain sign-as team.testnet network-config testnet sign-with-keychain send
2. Use function-call access keys, never full-access keys, on agent hosts - A function-call access key can only call the listed contract and cannot transfer NEAR or deploy code, which limits the blast radius. Command: near account add-key agent.team.testnet grant-function-call-access --allowance '0.25 NEAR' --contract-account-id hub.team.testnet --function-names 'place_bid, submit_work' autogenerate-new-keypair save-to-keychain network-config testnet sign-with-keychain send
3. Restrict method names on every function-call key - Method restrictions mean a leaked worker key cannot call verify_bounty or select_winner; list only the methods the role needs and test that other calls fail.
4. Set a gas allowance on each key - Allowance limits cap how much gas a stolen key can burn. The allowance cannot be raised later, so rotate the key when it runs out instead of granting an unlimited allowance.
5. Remove full-access keys after setup - Removing full-access keys from agent sub-accounts means the only remaining key is the restricted one. Command: near account delete-keys agent.team.testnet public-keys ed25519:<pk> network-config testnet sign-with-keychain send. Keep recovery on the parent account.
6. Rotate keys on a schedule and after incidents - Key rotation: add the new function-call key with near-api-js account.addFunctionCallAccessKey(), switch the agent over, then delete the old key so a leaked key has a short lifetime.
7. Keep secrets out of the repository - Load private keys from environment variables (.env.local, gitignored) and ship only .env.example; judges and attackers both scan git history.
8. Plan sub-account deletion and fund recovery - Sub-account deletion with a beneficiary returns leftover NEAR to the parent: near account delete-account agent.team.testnet beneficiary team.testnet network-config testnet sign-with-keychain send.
sections.summary: Autonomous agents should hold the least privilege possible: one sub-account each, a function-call access key with method restrictions and an allowance, no full-access keys on the agent host, and a key rotation and deletion plan. Each item below names the risk it mitigates and a concrete near-cli-rs command or near-api-js call.
